A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HoT and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–R. Corresponding material can be matched despite extensive reformatting and substantive additions in v4.

before.justification: v3 reports original LLM benchmark results, hallucination measurements, ablations, and a 63-participant verification study, with additional empirical analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these empirical results and adds ReasoningTrap evaluations, advanced-prompting comparisons, fine-tuning experiments, and attention-entropy measurements.

M1.justification: Fine-tuning was future work in v3. Section 5.6 of v4 introduces supervised training on HoT responses for Llama-3.2-1B and Qwen-2.5-1.5B, enabling highlighted answers without few-shot demonstrations. Section 5.3 also introduces ComplexHoT. The original XML-based prompting procedure remains.

E1.justification: v4 adds PuzzleTrivial and conditioned AIME/MATH500 tasks that test adherence to unusual constraints rather than familiar solution templates, including their use in OOD evaluation. GSM8K disappears from the main arithmetic comparison but remains in appendix experiments, so its coverage is not wholly removed.

E2.justification: v4 adds ComplexCoT to the retained comparison in Table 8 and evaluates Least-to-Most, Tree-of-Thought, Self-Refine, and CoVE against HoT on r-GSM, Seven Objects, and Date in Table 9. Table 11 introduces base-model and CoT-fine-tuned controls for HoT fine-tuning.

E3.justification: New protocols train two small models on 3,187 examples per training condition and evaluate them on five OOD tasks. v4 also introduces response-unanimity and attention-entropy metrics and a three-dataset advanced-prompting comparison. The retained eight-shot evaluations and human-study procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: v4 adds response-consistency analysis in Table 2, contradiction and answer-omission findings in Section 5.2, and an attention-entropy comparison of fine-tuned models in Table 12. Appendix N adds StrategyQA, PuzzleTrivial, and MATH500 cases. Existing component, tag-format, mismatched-tag, and LLM-judge analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report five independent runs and mean ± standard deviation for repeated prompting comparisons, alongside human-study variability. The additional comparison follows that existing reporting practice. No new seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or explicit increase in run counts is reported.

E6.justification: v4 adds consistency, ReasoningTrap, advanced-prompting, fine-tuning, and entropy results. Table 8 adds ComplexCoT and ComplexHoT means of 86.45 and 88.54. The arithmetic improvement summary changes from +2.10 to +2.61 because the GSM8K column is omitted; shared per-task scores and human-study results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix D adds mathematical definitions of the final-layer attention matrix, content/tag token sets, and per-head and head-averaged attention scores, previously described only verbally. Appendix C's human-verification formula is retained. No theorem, proof, or formal performance guarantee is added.

C1.justification: v4's contributions now include superiority over several advanced prompting methods, compatibility with ComplexCoT, and improved small-model OOD accuracy through HoT fine-tuning. The abstract changes its coverage claim from 20 to 22 tasks. The introduction also drops v3's 'estimated' qualifier from the human-verification accuracy claim.

C2.justification: v4 distinguishes SelfCheckGPT consistency from answer correctness and interprets new OOD gains through better use of input facts. Appendix D adds a hypothesis that tag embeddings carry enclosed information. Limitations newly address repetition-token and annotation costs, while explicit LaTeX/code and medical/multimodal caveats disappear. Human-overtrust concerns remain elsewhere.

D1.justification: Appendix D newly specifies attention extraction and aggregation details. Section 5.6 identifies Gemini-1.5-Pro as the training-data generator and supplies corpus counts. Existing API configurations and prompting materials remain. The new fine-tuning study does not provide optimizer, learning-rate, epoch, or hardware details.

R1.justification: v4 adds focused engagement with advanced prompting methods, ReasoningTrap, small-model references, attention sinks, and vision-transformer registers. These support the new experiments and mechanism hypothesis. The established positioning relative to document citations, RAG, span prediction, and human highlighting research remains largely intact.

P1.justification: v4 rewrites selected results and limitations passages, revises section titles, and merges discussion and conclusion. Trung Bui is added to the author list and the acknowledgments are removed. Most existing method, related-work, and appendix prose is retained.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, with document-wide typography, caption, and placement changes. Opening illustrations are replaced with new examples, new experimental tables are added, the prompting-comparison table gains columns, and the arithmetic table loses its GSM8K column. Appendix tables and figures are extensively reflowed.

improvement.justification: Broader comparator tests, fine-tuning/OOD experiments, and clearer measurement discussion address gaps in v3. However, new central results are inconsistent: Table 3's displayed scores imply about +9.00 points rather than +11.38, and Table 11's Llama-HoT row averages 25.01 rather than 27.02. These unresolved discrepancies and missing fine-tuning settings weaken the added evidence, preventing a confident judgment of net overall improvement.
